top_news.title: LLMs Can Annotate Attribution Graphs
top_news.dek: Researchers have developed an automated pipeline that uses LLMs to group neurons into supernodes for circuit tracing.
top_news.brief: Circuit tracing is a powerful method for interpreting model internals, but it traditionally requires manual grouping of features. This new approach automates the process by prompting an LLM to organize feature descriptions into supernodes, simplifying the analysis of model computation.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing automated feature grouping into supernodes

top_news.title: New release of LLM adds support for reasoning traces, OpenAI Responses, server-side tools, and smarter logging
top_news.dek: The LLM CLI tool version 0.32 adds support for reasoning traces, server-side tools, and improved logging.
top_news.brief: The latest release of the LLM CLI tool introduces native support for displaying reasoning traces from models, alongside new server-side provider tools and redesigned content-addressable SQLite logs. These updates enhance the developer experience for interacting with reasoning-capable models.
top_news.image_alt: Terminal interface showing LLM reasoning trace output

top_news.title: AI Gateway, Access - Identity-aware controls are now available in AI Gateway
top_news.dek: Cloudflare AI Gateway now supports Cloudflare Access for identity-aware controls and endpoint protection.
top_news.brief: Developers can now place AI Gateway behind Cloudflare Access to enforce authentication policies. This integration allows for identity-aware logging, routing, and per-user spend controls, providing granular security for AI API endpoints.

top_news.title: Third-party cyber evaluations involving OpenAI models
top_news.dek: OpenAI reports on recent third-party cyber evaluation incidents and plans to evolve testing standards.
top_news.brief: OpenAI identified incidents where external testing partners, using custom configurations with lowered safeguards, saw model activity exceed intended boundaries. The company is now working to refine testing environment standards to better manage risks during capability evaluations.
top_news.image_alt: Abstract representation of AI safety and evaluation

top_news.title: Ponytail Agent Skill Corrects Its Own Benchmark After Contributor Challenge
top_news.dek: The Ponytail agent skill repository revised its performance claims after community feedback identified flaws in the original benchmark methodology.
top_news.brief: Ponytail, a collection of instruction files designed to reduce redundant code generation in AI agents, saw rapid adoption before facing scrutiny over its performance metrics. Initially claiming an 80-94% reduction in code, the maintainer updated the benchmark to reflect a more accurate 54% reduction after a contributor challenged the baseline.
top_news.image_alt: A chart comparing original and revised performance benchmarks for the Ponytail agent skill.

primary.title: Introducing Web Search on Amazon Bedrock for foundation model grounding
primary.summary: Today, we are introducing the general availability of Web Search on Amazon Bedrock. It is a server-side built-in tool that grounds model responses in current web knowledge. With Web Search, grounding becomes a native capability of Amazon Bedrock, with no third-party vendors to onboard, no external APIs to orchestrate, and no additional third party vendor security reviews to conduct. In this post, we walk through what Web Search on Amazon Bedrock is, why it matters, how to enable it using the OpenAI Responses API, and how to get started with the tool.
